anomalies.observed: In the netlist, U10.4 (GND1) and U10.5 (GND2) are both connected to the GND net; the same applies to U11.4 and U11.5. The isolated CAN transceivers' logic-side and bus-side grounds are tied together.
anomalies.expected: Isolated CAN transceivers require separate ground nets for the logic side (GND1) and the bus side (GND2) to maintain galvanic isolation. The specification states the CAN buses are 'isolated CAN buses'.

evidence.quote: GND [High Power] : ... U10.4(GND1,power_in) U10.5(GND2,power_in) ... U11.4(GND1,power_in) U11.5(GND2,power_in)
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation between the CAN bus and the rest of the board is completely defeated, creating ground loops and eliminating the protective isolation the design intended.

anomalies.observed: U13.9 (I2C/~SPI) and U14.9 are tied to GND, selecting I2C mode. However, the surrounding pins are wired for SPI: U13.13 (SCL/SCLK) to SERIAL_CLK, U13.11 (A1/SI) to SERIAL_COPI, U13.12 (SO) to SERIAL_CIPO, U13.10 (A0/~CS) to CS1. Additionally, U13.14 (SDA/VSS) is grounded; in I2C mode this pin is SDA.
anomalies.expected: For SPI operation (as evidenced by the SPI signal connections), pin 9 (I2C/~SPI) must be tied high (e.g., to SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V). In I2C mode, pin 14 would be SDA and must not be grounded.
anomalies.impact: The SC16IS752 UART bridges are configured for I2C mode but wired for SPI, and in I2C mode their SDA pin is shorted to ground. They will not communicate, rendering the serial ports non-functional.

anomalies.observed: U29 is a non-inverting buffer (SN74LVC1G07 or U74LVC1G125). Its input A (pin 2) is tied to the +5V rail. Its output Y (pin 4) drives the gate of P-channel MOSFET Q9, whose gate also has pull-up resistor R48 to +5V. Because U29's input is tied high, its output can only be high (1G125) or high-impedance (1G07), so Q9's gate is always high (off).
anomalies.expected: To turn on P-MOSFET Q9, its gate must be pulled low. The buffer must be able to pull its output low when enabled, which requires its input A to be driven low (e.g., by 5V_CAN_ENABLE) or to use an inverting configuration.
anomalies.impact: Q9 never turns on, so the 5V_switched_CAN rail is never powered. The isolated side of the CAN transceivers (U10, U11) receives no power, making the CAN buses non-functional.

parsed.summary: The design files contain multiple serious anomalies. The most severe is that the isolated CAN transceivers have their logic-side and bus-side grounds tied together, completely defeating the intended galvanic isolation. Additionally, the SC16IS752 UART bridges are misconfigured for I2C while wired for SPI, and the P-MOSFET Q9 that powers the isolated CAN side can never turn on.
